# Calibration provenance

**This file is generated by `tools/gen_calibration_report.py` from the shipped configs. Do not edit
it by hand.** `kubegym verify` regenerates it and fails on any difference, so the report cannot
drift from the constants the simulator actually uses.

## How to read it

Every physical constant carries four mandatory fields and two optional flags:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `value` | the constant in use |
| `calibrated` | `true` **only** if the value came from a measurement |
| `source` | how it was obtained: n, hardware, fit quality, or an explicit statement that it is a placeholder. A field without a source is refused at load time |
| `required_for_claims` | if `true`, a placeholder here makes the whole run non-reportable |
| `weak_evidence` | measured, but from too few observations to lean on |
| `flagged_optimistic` | known to bias results favourably; the source states in which direction |

**The claims gate.** A configuration reports `calibrated = false` if *any* field marked
`required_for_claims` is still a placeholder. That flag is stamped onto every result row the
environment produces, so a number carrying `calibrated=false` is a comparison inside an
uncalibrated simulator and **is not an empirical performance claim**. Nothing in the codebase
upgrades a placeholder to measured except an explicit `override(..., attest=...)` that records the
new measurement in the provenance block.

## `llm_serving_l40s.json`

Claims gate: **`calibrated = False`**.

Blocked by these placeholder fields marked `required_for_claims`: `decode_batch_extrapolation_above_8`, `output_length_distribution`, `prefill_tokens_per_s`, `slo`.

| constant | value | status | flags | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chunked_prefill` | `False` | **placeholder** | - | NOT MODELLED. vLLM v1 enables chunked prefill by default; the simulator charges a whole-prompt prefill that stalls the replica's decode. This overstates the TBT spike caused by an admission and understates the TTFT of a long prompt under load. |
| `class_predictor_accuracy` | `1` | **placeholder** | - | Sensitivity knob, not a measurement. 1.0 = the controller reads thinking_mode as-is. Below 1.0 the class signal handed to belief-based controllers is corrupted with that per-request probability of being correct, standing in for a real prompt-length predictor's error. |
| `class_signal` | `thinking_mode` | measured | - | The router genuinely observes `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking` on every request, so conditioning a belief on thinking mode uses no privileged information. CAVEAT, see controllers_report.md 6.2: in the emitted traces thinking_flip_prob=0.0, so thinking_mode is a NOISELESS proxy for the length class. Set class_predictor_accuracy < 1.0 to inject predictor error. |
| `control_interval_s` | `15` | measured | - | Matches the Kubernetes HPA default sync period (--horizontal-pod-autoscaler-sync-period, default 15 s) so that the HPA baseline runs at its real cadence. All controllers are given the same decision cadence. |
| `decode_batch_extrapolation_above_8` | `affine` | **placeholder** | required for claims, flagged optimistic | PLACEHOLDER / UNVERIFIED. Throughput was measured only at batch 1, 4 and 8. Above batch 8 the simulator extrapolates the affine step-time model, which predicts near-linear aggregate throughput (e.g. 872 tok/s at batch 16, 1591 tok/s at batch 32). Real engines saturate; the affine extrapolation is therefore OPTIMISTIC about large batches and biases the simulator toward under-provisioning being cheap. Must be measured at batch 16/32/64 before any claim. |
| `decode_step_time_s` | `a0_s=0.01657539, a1_s_per_seq=0.00011063` | measured | required for claims | LEAST-SQUARES FIT to measured single-replica decode throughput from vLLM's own iteration logger: 60.3 / 232.6 / 460.2 tok/s at 1 / 4 / 8 concurrent requests. Model t_step(b) = a0 + a1*b seconds per scheduler step, where one step emits one token for each of the b running sequences. Max relative error on the three fitted points: 1.05%.  (max_rel_err_on_fit_points=0.0105) |
| `gpu_cost_per_replica_hour_usd` | `1` | **placeholder** | - | NORMALISED UNIT, not a price quote. Cost is reported primarily as replica-seconds (GPU-seconds); the USD column is replica-hours x 1.0 so it is a pure rescaling. Substitute a real instance price only when quoting money. |
| `kv_tokens_per_replica` | `55200` | measured | required for claims | MEASURED on the GPU testbed: KV budget per replica at --gpu-memory-utilization 0.21, vLLM 0.25.1, Qwen3-1.7B. |
| `max_num_seqs` | `256` | **placeholder** | - | PLACEHOLDER: vLLM's documented default max_num_seqs. Not read off the live server config. In practice KV pressure binds before this does at these sequence lengths. |
| `metric_scrape_interval_s` | `15` | **placeholder** | - | Design choice matching the control interval. On the real testbed this is the Prometheus scrape interval and introduces staleness the simulator currently models as zero. |
| `n_replicas_max` | `4` | measured | required for claims | GPU testbed track: 4 co-resident vLLM replicas on one L40S 46GB, each --gpu-memory-utilization 0.21, --max-model-len 8192. |
| `n_replicas_min` | `1` | measured | - | Design choice: at least one replica must serve. |
| `output_length_distribution` | `length_model.py` | **placeholder** | required for claims | Delegated to length_model.py, which returns calibrated:false and the labelled placeholder lognormals until measured_lengths.json lands. THIS IS THE DOMINANT UNCALIBRATED INPUT: it sets the offered token load. |
| `preemption_policy` | `recompute` | **placeholder** | - | Models vLLM's recompute-style preemption: a preempted sequence returns to the head of the waiting queue and re-pays prefill on its already-generated prefix. Output tokens are not lost (deterministic-decode assumption). vLLM's exact victim-selection order was NOT read from source; the simulator preempts the most-recently-admitted sequence. |
| `prefill_tokens_per_s` | `6000` | **placeholder** | required for claims | PLACEHOLDER, NOT MEASURED. Prompt-prefill throughput was never measured on the testbed. Governs TTFT and the decode stall a new admission causes. Any TTFT number from this simulator is placeholder-derived. |
| `replica_bringup` | `sequential` | measured | - | VERIFIED OPERATIONAL CONSTRAINT on the GPU testbed: starting several vLLM engines concurrently fails KV sizing, so replicas were brought up ONE AT A TIME. The pool therefore serialises boots: the i-th replica requested at t becomes ready at max(t, last_pending_ready) + replica_cold_start_s. This is a lifecycle policy, not a measured scalar; `calibrated: true` records that the sequential path is the one that was actually exercised, not that a timing was fitted. |
| `replica_cold_start_s` | `31.9` | measured | required for claims | MEASURED, n=9: median 31.90 s to serving-ready, IQR [31.82, 32.40]. This is the actuation lag d.  (n=9; iqr_s=[31.82, 32.4]) |
| `replica_teardown_s` | `0.54` | measured | weak evidence | MEASURED but n=2 only (0.54 s for 1 replica, 1.31 s for 4 concurrent). TREAT AS AN UPPER BOUND / weak evidence.  (n=2) |
| `router_policy` | `least_running` | **placeholder** | - | PLACEHOLDER for the real router's balancing policy: dispatch to the READY replica with the fewest running+waiting requests. The real router's policy must be recorded and matched here before any claim. |
| `slo` | `ttft_p95_s=2.0, tbt_p95_s=0.05, ttft_hard_s=5.0` | **placeholder** | required for claims | DESIGN CHOICE pending calibration, not a measurement. tbt_p95_s = 0.05 s (20 tok/s per stream) sits above the measured single-stream 58 tok/s, so it is reachable; ttft targets are provisional and must be set from the measured single-replica capacity curve. |

## `request_service_default.json`

Claims gate: **`calibrated = False`**.

Blocked by these placeholder fields marked `required_for_claims`: `replica_cold_start_s`, `rs_max_concurrency`, `rs_service_time_distribution`, `slo`.

| constant | value | status | flags | source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `control_interval_s` | `15` | measured | - | Matches the Kubernetes HPA default sync period (--horizontal-pod-autoscaler-sync-period, default 15 s) so the HPA baseline runs at its real cadence. All controllers get the same decision cadence. |
| `cost_per_replica_hour_usd` | `1` | **placeholder** | - | NORMALISED UNIT, not a price quote. Cost is reported primarily as replica-seconds; the USD column is replica-hours x 1.0, a pure rescaling. Substitute a real instance price only when quoting money. |
| `metric_scrape_interval_s` | `15` | **placeholder** | flagged optimistic | Design choice matching the control interval. On a real platform this is the metrics scrape period and introduces staleness that this model currently treats as zero, which is OPTIMISTIC about the controller's information. |
| `n_replicas_max` | `20` | **placeholder** | - | PLACEHOLDER. Arbitrary ceiling chosen so that a scale-out range exists for RL action spaces; it is NOT the capacity of any real platform. Unlike the LLM config's n_replicas_max=4, this is not a physical limit that was measured, so a target near it is not automatically hypothetical. |
| `n_replicas_min` | `1` | measured | - | Design choice: at least one replica must serve. Not a measurement. |
| `replica_bringup` | `parallel` | **placeholder** | - | PLACEHOLDER / design choice. Container platforms start replicas concurrently, so parallel bring-up is the plausible default here -- unlike the LLM config, where concurrent engine init was verified to fail KV sizing and sequential bring-up is the verified path. Not measured. |
| `replica_cold_start_s` | `2` | **placeholder** | required for claims | PLACEHOLDER, NOT MEASURED. A round 2 s stand-in for container cold start. Real serverless cold starts span roughly two orders of magnitude across runtimes and platforms, and the value dominates every scale-up decision, so this is the single most important constant to replace before any claim. |
| `replica_teardown_s` | `0.5` | **placeholder** | - | PLACEHOLDER, NOT MEASURED. Not billed by default (see kubegym/core/replica.py), so it currently affects nothing; kept so the field exists when teardown billing is switched on. |
| `router_policy` | `least_running` | **placeholder** | - | PLACEHOLDER for a real load balancer's policy: dispatch to the READY replica with the fewest running+waiting requests. See kubegym/core/router.py for the alternatives. |
| `rs_contention_slowdown` | `0` | **placeholder** | flagged optimistic | PLACEHOLDER, NOT MEASURED. Per-request service rate is 1/(1 + slowdown*(b-1)) with b in service. The default 0.0 means concurrency slots are perfectly independent, so a loaded replica is as fast as an idle one. That is the OPTIMISTIC end: it makes under-provisioning look cheaper than it would be on real shared-CPU hardware. Set >0 for a pessimistic sensitivity arm. |
| `rs_max_concurrency` | `4` | **placeholder** | required for claims | PLACEHOLDER, NOT MEASURED. Requests served simultaneously per replica; the rest queue FIFO. Round number chosen to be obviously synthetic. This is the binding capacity constant of the model, analogous to kv_tokens_per_replica in the LLM model. |
| `rs_queue_discipline` | `fifo` | **placeholder** | - | Design choice, not a measurement: per-replica FIFO with an unbounded queue, no admission control, no timeouts, no drops. Real platforms shed load; this model does not, which makes queueing delay the only visible symptom of overload. |
| `rs_service_time_distribution` | `family=lognormal, mu=0.0, sigma=1.0` ... | **placeholder** | required for claims | PLACEHOLDER, NOT MEASURED. Lognormal with mu=0, sigma=1 on the natural-log scale of seconds (median 1.0 s, mean about 1.65 s, CV about 1.31) -- deliberately round parameters, not an estimate of any workload. Drawn once per request at episode build time so controller comparisons are paired. Tail heaviness (sigma) is the parameter that decides whether capacity planning is hard at all, so it must not be treated as an empirical choice. When a replay trace supplies a measured service_time_s per record, that value is used verbatim and this field is not consulted. |
| `slo` | `latency_p95_s=1.0, latency_hard_s=5.0, queue_delay_p95_s=0.5` | **placeholder** | required for claims | DESIGN CHOICE pending calibration, not a measurement. Provisional targets so the cost-SLO objective is well defined. They must be identical across controllers in any comparison. |

## What a `calibrated=false` run is good for, and what it is not

It is good for *relative, paired* comparison inside the simulator: every controller faces the same
arrival and service realisation on a given episode, so a controller-versus-controller contrast is
not confounded by workload sampling. It supports statements of the form "under this model, method A
costs less than method B on this workload family, by this margin, with this dispersion".

It does **not** support statements about production behaviour. Simulation fidelity is a property of
the model structure and of the interactions between constants, not of the constants taken one at a
time, so even a fully "calibrated" configuration would not establish sim-to-real transfer. There is
no sim-to-real validation study here, and every claim is scoped to in-simulator comparison.

## The measurement campaign behind the measured constants

The constants marked measured in `llm_serving_l40s.json` come from a prior measurement campaign on a
single-GPU testbed: four co-resident vLLM replicas on one NVIDIA L40S (46 GB), vLLM 0.25.1, each
replica at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.22`. Cold start is a median over n=9 launches; the decode
step-time model is a least-squares fit to throughput measured at batch 1, 4 and 8 (maximum relative
error 1.05% on the fit points); the KV budget was read from the engine's own reported cache size;
and the replica ceiling of 4 is the physical limit at which a fifth engine fails KV sizing.

Constants that campaign did **not** establish are labelled placeholders here rather than filled in
with plausible values. The three that matter most, all `required_for_claims`:

* `prefill_tokens_per_s` — never measured. Every time-to-first-token number is placeholder-derived.
* `decode_batch_extrapolation_above_8` — throughput was measured only to batch 8; above it the model
  extrapolates affinely. Real engines saturate, so this is **optimistic**: it makes
  under-provisioning look cheaper than it is.
* `output_length_distribution` — a labelled placeholder lognormal. This one sets the difficulty of
  the whole control problem and is the dominant uncalibrated input.

`request_service_default.json` is a modelling scaffold, not a calibrated artifact: every one of its
physical constants is a placeholder, and it is the configuration the Azure Functions corpus runs on.
Its `control_interval_s` and `n_replicas_min` are the only fields marked measured, and both are
conventions — the Kubernetes HPA default sync period, and the requirement that at least one replica
serve — rather than measurements of any service.
